sub: They said someone had emptied it — the earliest answer
on record, written in Matthew's own Gospel. (Matthew 28:13)
thread:
You are not the first person to ask.

The hardest question you have about the Christian faith is almost certainly older than you think.

Here is the earliest answer Jesus' opponents gave — and where it is written down. 🧵

Open Matthew 28. The charge is right there in the text:

"His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep." (Matthew 28:13)

Read it again. His opponents did not say the grave was full. They said someone had emptied it.

The church did not bury that.

It wrote it down — inside its own Gospel, in the account it was circulating.

Around AD 160, Justin Martyr names the same charge, still circulating generations later (Dialogue with Trypho 108).

He does not dodge it. He names it.

Around AD 248, Origen answers the philosopher Celsus — who had written some seventy years earlier — point by point, across eight books.

He quotes Celsus so fully that most of Celsus' own work survives only inside the reply that answers it.

Twenty centuries, and the pattern never changes.

Every generation brings its hardest question. Every generation answers it in writing.

That charge was never hidden. It is printed in Matthew's own Gospel.

That is what Asked & Answered is: 102 questions, answered plainly, every one reviewed for orthodoxy with the date on the record.

Bring the question you have been carrying. It has been asked before. Here is our answer.
